title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that isolates downstream deterministic validation and a bounded repair budget under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes) and a deterministic digital‑twin validator, we compared a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator to a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage. Declared model/provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses); validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; only deterministic validation and up to one permitted repair (guarded arm) could change paired outcomes. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar as the confirmatory outcome, label the one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc (it was not prespecified), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Motivation and problem framing. Translating operator intent into executable network configuration actions is a core NetOps workload. Generative LLMs can accelerate intent→configuration translation but introduce operational risk: multi‑step ordering errors, transient invariant violations (e.g., bringing redundant paths down), and inadvertent edits to protected fields. Prior literature documents hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures for code and configuration generation; these findings motivate architectures that pair generation with deterministic validation and bounded repair to improve operational safety [1],[2].

Study focus and estimand. We designed a narrowly scoped, preregistered paired study whose estimand isolates downstream interventions only: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate (preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate), to what degree does a deterministic validator plus at most one permitted repair (guarded pipeline with canary) improve the paired safe‑deploy rate relative to reusing the same initial candidate without repair (baseline)? Under shared_initial_candidate semantics any paired difference can arise only from deterministic validator decisions and the permitted repair(s); the design therefore measures the incremental effect of post‑generation validation/repair rather than effects of prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or independent first‑pass re‑generation.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered confirmatory paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) with complete archived execution and analysis artifacts; (2) precise, artifact‑grounded outcome accounting showing baseline = 995/1000 and guarded = 1000/1000 with five repairs invoked; (3) interpretation reconciling preregistered power assumptions with the observed near‑unity baseline and sparse discordant counts; (4) operationally relevant recommendations for follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, validator coverage, and repair budgets.
sections.related_work:
LLM failures and structured outputs. Broad empirical surveys and task‑specific studies document hallucination, high prompt sensitivity, and correctness failures when LLMs produce structured artifacts such as code or configuration templates; these failures materially affect downstream executability and safety [1],[2]. Studies of constrained decoding and schema‑aware generation show improvements in syntactic and executability metrics in structured domains, though much primary evidence originates outside NetOps and effectiveness depends on the quality of schema enforcement [3],[4].

Generate→validate→repair and verifier‑assisted architectures. System and benchmark papers in NetOps and adjacent domains describe guarded pipelines that pair generation with validators or digital twins and permit bounded repairs or operator‑in‑the‑loop approvals; prototype evaluations report correctness gains but emphasize dependence on validator fidelity, coverage, and protocol governance rather than on any single model alone [5],[6],[7]. Our work complements these by preregistering a paired experiment that fixes the initial candidate and thereby isolates whether downstream deterministic validation and one allowed repair can produce measurable paired improvements under tightly controlled conditions.

Gap and positioning. Existing benchmarks often score first‑pass correctness or measure unconstrained generation across models. A workflow‑centered evaluation that accounts for trace quality, canary/rollback outcomes, and the marginal effect of verifier/repair layers under shared_initial_candidate semantics is less common. We contribute an artifact‑grounded study that fills this gap for a narrowly specified estimand, and we preserve all preregistered artifacts and execution traces for reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. The study was preregistered (cand‑003‑stud‑001) and frozen before any hosted‑model invocation; the preregistration SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest (ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered elements: paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar on 2×2 paired contingency table. Secondary preregistered summaries included a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and sensitivity analyses treating failed calls as unsafe.

Task corpus, validator, and scoring. Tasks were selected deterministically by the preregistered ordinal rule producing 1000 unique task indices. Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (very_hard, extreme). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a digital‑twin emulator that deterministically parses candidate command sequences, enforces required sequence/order constraints, protected‑field noninterference, and other workflow policies, and returns a binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest. Scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation produced the binary outcomes used in the paired analysis. Representative validator traces and response files are archived in execution/scoring and execution/responses.

Generation semantics and interpretive consequences. The preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate implies one sampled initial generation (shared) per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes; thus only deterministic validation and permitted repair(s) can change paired outcomes. This design isolates downstream verifier/repair efficacy but does not measure generation or prompt/decoding interventions that require independent initial samples. We emphasize this interpretive boundary throughout.

Model configuration and temperature caveat. Declared model/provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task was produced and shared across conditions (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) per the preregistration.

Execution accounting, retries, and missingness. The adapter/executor contract limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 2000, completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}, and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false. The preregistered missingness_plan specified 'complete_pair_primary' treatment for incomplete pairs; no failed episodes occurred and no post‑hoc exclusions were applied.

Statistical analysis plan and prespecification fidelity. The preregistered confirmatory procedure was the exact two‑sided McNemar test on the 2×2 paired contingency table. The paired bootstrap percentile interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was preregistered as a descriptive secondary summary. Reviewer‑requested clarification: an exact one‑sided McNemar test was NOT prespecified in the frozen preregistration; any one‑sided computation reported here is explicitly exploratory/post‑hoc.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting (artifact‑grounded). Run start/completion: 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z → 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed episodes = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; cache_miss_count = 1005; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}. Total model calls used = 1005. All deterministic consistency checks passed.

Primary paired outcomes. The preregistered paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Inferential results (preregistered tests). The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test yields p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05, so preregistered H1 is not supported. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The bootstrap CI was preregistered as descriptive; it excludes zero because resampling with extremely sparse discordant pairs can produce nonzero percentile bounds. A one‑sided McNemar test (exploratory/post‑hoc) yields p = 0.03125; because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration it is explicitly reported as exploratory.

Repair mechanics and representative artifacts. Repair stage_count = 5 (only five validator‑triggered repairs invoked). Representative episode artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task‑000004‑*.json) show the shared initial candidate rejected by the validator due to required_sequence or protected_interface violations, a single permitted repair call invoked by the guarded adapter, and subsequent validator acceptance of the repaired candidate. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces, and validator traces are archived in the execution evidence bundle; example response digests and validator final_state snapshots are present in execution/scoring artifacts.

Contamination, exclusions, and missingness. The preregistered contamination checks found no prompt‑leakage flags; contamination_summary.csv is empty. Missingness_summary.csv reports zero failed or unscorable episodes. No post‑hoc exclusions were applied. All task selection seeds and index rules were fixed prior to execution as specified in the preregistration.

Quantitative sensitivity diagnostics. The extreme concentration of successes (995/1000 baseline) yields sparse discordant counts (only five n10). This data regime reduces the sensitivity of discrete paired tests to detect small absolute improvements: the preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈0.60 and target effect ≈0.15; with the observed baseline near unity the realized effective power to detect a 0.005 absolute effect is negligible. Bootstrap summaries remain informative descriptively but must be interpreted with caution under sparse discordance.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive interpretation. The preregistered confirmatory outcome is the two‑sided exact McNemar (p = 0.0625) and therefore does not support H1 at α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a preregistered descriptive summary and excludes zero due to bootstrap behavior with sparse discordant pairs; it does not override the preregistered confirmatory test. A one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory.

Power assumptions mismatch and consequences. The preregistered power_and_precision_plan targeted an absolute effect of 0.15 assuming baseline ≈0.60; the observed baseline success rate (0.995) violates that assumption, dramatically reducing sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. This mismatch is artifact‑grounded (power_and_precision_plan in the preregistration) and explains why the confirmatory test is non‑significant despite a nonzero paired difference. Readers should therefore interpret non‑significance in context: the study lacked power to detect very small absolute improvements given near‑unity baseline validity.

Mechanistic implications of shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms reused the identical initial generation, any observed paired improvement derives solely from deterministic validation and the limited repair budget. The five successful repairs demonstrate that a validator with appropriate coverage can correct certain ordering/sequence or protected‑field violations. However, the small repair count limits inferences about repair throughput, failure‑class coverage, and marginal returns of additional repair budget. Detecting effects of prompt engineering, constrained decoding, or repeated independent first‑pass sampling requires independent generation arms not executed here.

Construct and external validity threats. Construct validity depends on validator coverage: the safe‑deploy binary is only as meaningful as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule completeness. If the validator omits semantic policy checks or emergent multi‑device conditions, measured success rates overstate operational safety. External validity is limited by single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic task corpus, and a deterministic digital twin; heterogeneity in vendor devices, OSs, and real telemetry may alter both generator behavior and validator sensitivity.

Operational implications and recommended follow‑ups. Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and repair budget. Recommended preregistered follow‑ups: (1) run a non‑shared generation arm (independent first‑pass generations per condition) to measure prompt/decoding interventions; (2) sweep repair budgets (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns by failure class; (3) expand validator rule sets and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) evaluate multiple model families to assess model dependence. Each follow‑up should include power plans aligned to realistic baseline failure rates and prespecified analysis choices.

Best practices for workflow‑centered NetOps evaluation. Our experiment highlights three practices: preregister paired estimands that explicitly declare generation semantics (shared vs independent), archive deterministic validator traces and provider call audits to enable mechanistic accounting, and align power calculations with realistic baseline failure prevalence. These practices make apparent why some confirmatory tests lack sensitivity and prevent conflation of downstream corrections with first‑pass generation improvements.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired study (cand‑003‑stud‑001) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus using shared_initial_candidate semantics, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The study's shared_initial_candidate design isolates downstream validation/repair effects, but the near‑unity baseline and sparse discordant counts limit inferential sensitivity. All preregistration, execution manifests, raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and guide preregistered follow‑ups that expand model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus (challenging_workflow_stress_v1) and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments and noisy telemetry is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations, constrained decoding, or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 0.995; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs: only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred, constraining inference about repair efficacy across diverse failure modes and limiting mechanistic generalization.

Construct validity dependency: the safe‑deploy binary depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). A paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] was preregistered as a descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory.
